external_entities.name: colleague
external_entities.description: A member of staff who signs in through the broker from wherever they are, including their own device at home, and then uses the applications the token admits them to.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

external_entities.name: franchise identity provider
external_entities.description: The franchise stores' own identity provider. It vouches for franchise colleagues and the broker takes that as a sign-in; nothing is written down about which colleagues it may vouch for.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in. We have not written down which colleagues that provider is allowed to vouch for.
external_entities.notes: Franchise colleagues themselves are not modelled: they have no account here, and how they reach their own provider is outside the system this model describes and unstated in the source.

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The system of record for group membership. The broker pulls changes from it once a night, and that is also how leavers stop being colleagues.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues twelve-hour tokens carrying staff id and group list, signs every application's tokens with one key, publishes the public half, pulls group changes from HR nightly and writes sign-ins to an audit log.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker. The broker runs on the corporate network.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: Lets the holder of a token carrying the store-manager group change prices and void transactions, without checking which store the colleague belongs to.
processes.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions. The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.
processes.notes: The source describes a class of applications that all take the token and decide from the groups in it, and names this one. It is modelled as the relying application: a second, nameless one would duplicate every flow the console already carries and add no stated fact.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The broker's own directory of colleagues and the groups they are in, populated overnight from the HR system.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: Holds the signing key. The same key signs the tokens for every application.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store. The same key signs the tokens for every application.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: Where the broker writes sign-ins. What it records, and whether it covers the franchise route, is not written down.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log. Nobody has written down what that log records, whether it covers the franchise route

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A colleague signs in to the broker from wherever they are; the token comes back on the same interaction.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
data_flows.data_description: the colleague's sign-in, and back to them a signed token carrying their staff id and group list, good for twelve hours with no way to pull it back before it expires

data_flows.name: vouch for colleague
data_flows.description: The franchise provider asserts a franchise colleague's identity and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in. We have not written down which colleagues that provider is allowed to vouch for.
data_flows.authentication: the broker accepts the provider's assertion as a sign-in; which colleagues the provider may vouch for is not written down
data_flows.data_description: an assertion vouching for a franchise colleague

data_flows.name: change prices and void
data_flows.description: The token holder changes prices and voids transactions in the console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.authentication: the token alone: its store-manager group decides, the colleague's own store is never checked, and nothing calls back to the broker to re-check them
data_flows.data_description: price changes and transaction voids against any store

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The application fetches the public half of the signing key from the broker to check token signatures.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: the public half of the token signing key

data_flows.name: nightly group pull
data_flows.description: The broker pulls group membership changes, leavers included, once a night.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night, and that is also how leavers stop being colleagues.
data_flows.data_description: group membership changes and leavers, applied once a night

data_flows.name: read write directory
data_flows.description: The broker reads colleagues and groups at sign-in and writes what the nightly pull brings back.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: read signing key
data_flows.description: The broker reads the one signing key it signs every application's tokens with.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: write sign ins
data_flows.description: The broker writes sign-ins to the log; what it writes is not stated.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: Where the broker, the store admin console, the directory, the key store and the audit log sit.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: outside corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: Wherever colleagues sign in from, their own devices at home included; the HR system is placed here for want of any stated location.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

trust_boundaries.name: franchise partner
trust_boundaries.description: The franchise stores and the identity provider they run; a separate party rather than a network location.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in. Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them

assumptions.assumption: The identity broker is reachable from outside the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: Colleagues are stated to sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home, while it is stated to run on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The franchise identity provider is a separate trust party from everywhere else outside the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The source introduces the franchise stores as a distinct group let in on distinct terms; it does not say where the provider runs, so the zone is drawn on the party rather than on a network.

assumptions.assumption: The HR system sits outside the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The source names it as the system of record the broker pulls from and never places it; grouped with the other unplaced parties rather than assumed internal.
